approach: Add `revert: bool` (serde default, skipped when false, like `reused`) to `CheckRun` in athena-data. In `crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs` add a pure `revert_record(group, run) -> CheckRun` that turns the finished demonstration run into a record: name `fails-without-N`, the plan's command, the exit code and output tail from the run, `revert = true`, and `passed = true` so it is never a blocking check. In `judge()`, inside the existing candidate_tree == checks_tree gate, add one rule: each `revert` record with an exit code adds its command (split by `simple_commands`) and its record name to `ran`. The current filter line `c.passed && (c.exit_code == Some(0) || (c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()))` stays byte for byte, because an admission test searches for that text. `demonstration_runs` / `demonstration_records` in `run/checks.rs` return the views together with the records; `verification_stage` appends the records to `check_runs` after the verifier's input view is built, so the brief is unchanged and the same list feeds `judge()` and `Verification.checks`. A group that did not run (not a plain cargo test, over the cap, scratch copy failed) yields a view only and no record. Every `CheckRun` literal gets `revert: false`. One filter in close.rs keeps the PR-body "N checks passed" count honest. CHANGELOG and job-planning.md are updated, and tests are added at the judge, run and record levels.

decisions.choice: Record a revert run as a CheckRun in verification.checks with a new `revert: bool` marker, and decide seen-running in judge().
decisions.reason: The request asks for the run to be in verification.json checks. `judge()` already reads `inputs.checks` under the tree-equality gate (verify.rs 374-382), so one rule beside it fixes the cause. Persisted records keep the evidence for maintainers. An optional field on an existing record needs no new record file, and `reused` is the precedent (records.rs 805-809).

rejected.option: Give judge() a separate list of demonstration runs outside checks
rejected.why: The request wants the run in the verification record's checks. A second list would add an input that the stored record could not reproduce.

rejected.option: Mark the record only by the name prefix `fails-without-`
rejected.why: A string convention is not a marker. Check names are free text, and a name rule could count a real check that happened to be called that.

decisions.choice: The revert record always has `passed = true`. It counts as seen running when `revert` is set and `exit_code.is_some()`, whatever the exit code.
decisions.reason: Existing readers treat `!passed` as a failed check: judge() blocking_checks (verify.rs 384), reading.rs 1585 and 1933, introspect.rs 939-949, and is_pre_existing. The existing comment on demonstration_view says a demonstration 'states no pass or fail of its own'. A nonzero exit is the expected result of a revert run, so it must not fail the verdict. A run that happened (exit code present) is seen running; the verifier judges what it showed.

rejected.why: A revert run that wrongly passes would then block the verdict and appear in 'failed check' carry text, which breaks the 'fails nothing' rule of 64cb889. A passing record would also take the old `exit_code == Some(0)` path in an unintended way.

rejected.option: Count only revert runs that exited nonzero
rejected.why: The request says to count the run regardless of the exit code. Whether the test failed is the verifier's judgement of the criterion, not a seen-running question.

decisions.choice: The revert rule sits inside the same `candidate_tree == checks_tree` gate, adds the record's command and its name to `ran`, and ignores records with no exit code.
decisions.reason: A record from another tree, or a placeholder or timed-out run, must never count. The gate and the exit-code test give exactly that. Adding the name lets a verifier cite `fails-without-1` as the brief shows it.

rejected.option: Count the record name for any record, run or not
rejected.why: A cited name that never ran would be seen running, which loosens D43 for criteria that do not cite a real run.

decisions.choice: Build the record in verify.rs with a pure `revert_record` function, next to demonstration_view, and call it from run/checks.rs.
decisions.reason: It keeps the field choices (name, command, marker, passed) in one place that unit tests can reach. checks.rs already overrides the shown command with the plan's text (line 350), and the record takes the same command.

rejected.option: Build the CheckRun inline in checks.rs
rejected.why: The judge tests would then need their own hand-made records, and nothing would tie the production shape to the test shape.

decisions.choice: Change the return type of demonstration_records and demonstration_runs to (views, runs). verification_stage extends `check_runs` after `inputs.checks` is built.
decisions.reason: inputs.checks is built from check_runs before the demonstration call (verification.rs 74-77 and 134). The verifier's brief therefore keeps the one 'not a check' view per run and nothing is shown twice. judge() (line 368) and Verification.checks (line 388) both read the extended list, so the verdict and the stored record agree.

rejected.option: Extend check_runs before building the verifier's inputs
rejected.why: The brief would show each run twice: as a check and as a demonstration.

decisions.choice: Do not add a refusal_corpus case.
decisions.reason: The rule is a verdict rule on commands the verifier cites, not a reading or plan refusal. I read refusal_corpus.rs: it has parser_cases, request_citing_cases, reading_check_cases, boundary_word_cases and plan_cases (ids such as dependents-missing), none of which touch judge(). The input forms of this rule (cited command, cited record name, not-run record, other tree, uncited command) are covered by the verify.rs tests.

rejected.option: Add corpus cases for the judge rule
rejected.why: The corpus runs reading and plan checks. The judge needs VerdictInputs, which the corpus has no harness for.

verify.rs: add `pub fn revert_record(group: &DemonstrationGroup, run: &CheckRun) -> CheckRun`. It copies the run and sets name `fails-without-<first criterion>`, command to the group's argv (or the plan's command split on whitespace), `revert = true`, `passed = true`, and `failed_tests` empty. Keep exit_code, tests_ran, duration, output_tail and note. Put it next to demonstration_view and give it a doc comment for an outside reader.

verify.rs judge(): leave the existing filter line as it is. Inside the `candidate_tree == checks_tree` block add a loop over `inputs.checks` with `c.revert && c.exit_code.is_some()` that extends `ran` with `simple_commands(&check.command.join(" "))` and pushes `check.name.clone()`. Comment that this counts for the 'fails without the fix' part, that a run that did not finish or is from another tree never counts, and that `passed` is always true so it never blocks.

run/checks.rs: make `demonstration_runs` return `(Vec<CheckResultView>, Vec<CheckRun>)` and `demonstration_records` the same pair. After each `run_check`, push `revert_record(g, &run)` to the second vector alongside the view; the not-run paths and the error path return an empty second vector. Update the doc comments: the view is shown to the verifier, the record is stored.

run/verification.rs: destructure `mut check_runs`. Replace `inputs.checks.extend(self.demonstration_records(...))` with `let (views, revert_runs) = self.demonstration_records(...); inputs.checks.extend(views); check_runs.extend(revert_runs);` and extend the comment saying why the order matters (inputs.checks was built from check_runs earlier, so nothing is shown twice).

Fix: each run is recorded as a revert-marked check and counts as seen running, for the 'fails without the fix' part only. docs/design/job-planning.md: add a paragraph after line 341 with the same scope in prose.

Run cargo test --locked -p athena-core verify, cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::, cargo test --locked -p athena-data, then cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check.

risks.risk: This loosens D43: a criterion citing the revert command could be counted as seen even though that run was on a reverted tree and failed.
risks.mitigation: Count a revert record only inside the tree-equality gate, only with an exit code, and only for its own command text and name. Record scope in the doc paragraph and the changelog. Tests for 'not run' and 'other tree' prove the limits; no other record kind is touched.

risks.risk: A nonzero exit, stored with passed = true, could still be read as a failed check by code that looks at exit codes.
risks.mitigation: The record is always passed = true, with tests that no blocking check or 'failed check' text comes from it. reading.rs, introspect.rs and judge() are listed in dependents with their tests.

risks.risk: About 51 CheckRun literals need the new field, and a missed one breaks the build.
risks.mitigation: Let the compiler find them: a missing field is a build error. Run cargo build --tests --locked after the edit to catch literals not in the listed files, such as gh/tests.rs or crates outside athena-core.

risks.risk: Editing the filter line in judge() breaks the admission test that searches verify.rs for it.
risks.mitigation: Keep the existing filter line unchanged and add a separate block. cargo test --locked runs the admission test.

risks.risk: The pull request body would say 'N checks passed' with the revert records included.
risks.mitigation: Filter revert records in close.rs and test the count.

risks.risk: check_minutes in status.rs sums all measured check durations, so the revert run adds to the job's check time.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: it is real time spent checking. A dependents entry records it, and the status tests run.

open_questions: User: Counting the revert run's command as seen running means a criterion that cites the same cargo test command as proof the test passes on the candidate would also be treated as seen, though that run was on the reverted tree. Should the command count only for a criterion whose demonstration has a fails_without? The reading has no fails_without field on a criterion, and the request lists adding one as out of scope, so the plan counts the command for any behavior criterion in the job.
